BRIDGE GIT RECONCILED TO LIVE 2026-05-23. While bumping the heartbeat version to match the stack (1.5.1), found the sovereign-bridge working tree was running roughly three minor versions ahead of git: HEAD was at v1.2.0 (commit 49cd49f) while the live process served 1.5.x with the legacy-token grace window, the /api/discover rewrite, and the comms-demote docstrings all uncommitted. Verified the running process started AFTER the on-disk edits (process start 2026-05-23 10:04 vs bridge.py mtime 2026-05-19), so the uncommitted code was already live, not pending deploy. HAZARD NAMED: uncommitted live code means any git checkout / branch-switch silently reverts the deployed bridge on the next restart. RESOLVED: committed the live state as a catch-up (commit 740d9a9) plus two reviewed auth-hardening fixes — (1) stop logging the expected-token prefix on mismatch (no secret to disk); (2) hmac.compare_digest on bytes for all three bearer comparisons (constant-time; bytes form so a non-ASCII Authorization header yields 403, not a 500). Fast-forwarded main 49cd49f -> 740d9a9 and pushed to origin (git@github.com:templetwo/sovereign-bridge.git). Now live == committed == main == origin. Heartbeat reads 1.5.1 / 82 tools / ok; authed /api/tools 200, no-auth /api/call 401, verified before and after the change.

OPEN FOLLOW-UPS (filed, non-blocking): (a) heartbeat recounts every comms jsonl with full read_text on each no-auth call — O(all comms) on the hottest unauthenticated endpoint, should be cached; (b) _record_legacy_caller does a blocking file write inside the async request path (rare, legacy-token only, but it is the blocking-in-event-loop pattern Sonnet fixed in April); (c) the Guardian feed writes a hand-rolled insight dict straight into ~/.sovereign/chronicle/insights/security,guardian,legacy-token bypassing record_insight (a second chronicle write path, the write-path-divergence pattern to watch); (d) bridge tests.py is stale (asserts 42 tools) and cannot serve as a commit gate as-is; (e) bridge VERSION is hand-synced to the stack version across two separate repos, which is how it drifted — deriving it from the stack would remove the manual step.

LESSON for future instances: both the sovereign-bridge and sovereign-stack repos have accumulated live-but-uncommitted state. Do not assume git HEAD reflects what is running. Check git status before reasoning about deployed behavior, and reconcile uncommitted live code into a commit so a branch-switch can never revert production.
